text:
rachel: follow-up from yesterday's RFC sync. proposing a prefix-sharded probe allocator that adds tenant-aware fairness + a minimal progress ramp for low-priority models. Goal: avoid KV poisoning and ensure every model makes measurable forward progress during onboarding rushes.

omar: prefixed sharding sounds promising. how do you map models to shards? hash(model_id)%N?

rachel: yes, default is consistent-hash(model_id)->shard. each shard gets a slice of the global probe_budget. shards enforce per-tenant soft floors and per-model ramps.

tessa: curious about tenant fairness math. do we weight by tenant commitments or by active model count?

rachel: primary weight = tenant_commitment (committed capacity), secondary = active_models. ranking formula: tenant_share = alpha * committed_capacity + beta * active_models_norm. Defaults: alpha=0.8 beta=0.2. insights welcome.

zane: prober-side: we should enforce a cap on unique prefixes in-flight (N_prefix_per_prober) and a TTL for buckets. Also prefer golden prefixes for sampling.

rachel: agreed. sketch of important knobs (toy config):
```json
{"onboard_pacer":"v0.3","global_budget_rps":"300","shards":64,"tenant_fairness":{"alpha":"0.8","beta":"0.2","min_tenant_floor_rps":"1"},"per_model":{"min_ramp_window_s":"600","min_probe_rps":"0.2"},"prober":{"max_unique_prefixes":"500","kv_safe_threshold":"0.7","golden_priority":true},"telemetry":{"emit_probe_plan_blob":true}
}
```

omar: what's the ramp behavior exactly? min_probe_rps is fraction of a probe-thread?

rachel: min_probe_rps is probes/sec floor per model (can be fractional). ramp_window_s is how long we linearly scale from min_probe_rps to allocated_probe_rps. prevents permanent starvation. e.g., min=0.2 rps, ramp=600s -> model gets 0.2 rps at t0, scales to target over 10m.

tessa: good. how do shards handle overloaded KV? eviction policy?

zane: two-bucket LRU: golden and "others". when kv_util>kv_safe_threshold, evict oldest from "others" first. also soft-cap unique prefixes; additional prefix attempts are delayed with exponential backoff per-model.

omar: what about dedicated pools? we must respect reservations. dedicated models should optionally be pinned to a shard that maps to dedicated capacity. override flag: deployment_hint=dedicated_reserved.

rachel: yes. intake will consult registry hints. if deployment_hint==dedicated_reserved and reserved_capacity >= required_capacity, we bypass shard-level soft throttle. otherwise still subject to shard fairness.

tessa: observability: we need to store the effective_probe_plan with the model entry (so audits and regressions can replay the conditions). plan should be compact: budget_rps, shard_id, ramp_window_s, min_probe_rps, kv_safe_threshold.

zane: also emit sample of prefix-eviction events to the bench telemetry so we can correlate metric skew with eviction spikes.

omar: simulation plan? I can assemble an ingest trace: multi-tenant hotspot, mixed seqlens, burst of 180 models in 12 minutes. include a tenant that both has high commit and a rogue tenant with many small models. we should compare variants: (A) no fairness, (B) tenant_fairness alpha=0.8, (C) alpha=0.5.

rachel: great. success criteria: (1) golden_coverage >=0.8 within 30m for 90% of models; (2) kv_miss_rate <5% overall; (3) median time-to-deepbench for low-priority <45m in rush; (4) no correctness-check failures attributable to pacing.

tessa: add secondary criteria: explainability of probe_plan in model registry UI and per-shard dashboards. SREs must be able to see which shard a model landed on and last N eviction events.

zane: implementation note: keep the intake shim simple: compute cost_score = recent_ingest_qps * expected_token_cost * seqlen_weight. default seqlen_weight table maintained in registry profiles. allow a model-level hint to override.

omar: edge case: models that declare extremely low expected_token_cost but blow up in practice. suggest we instrument a quick microbench (5 warmup requests) before full deepbench and escalate if observed cost > declared * factor. if so, reduce their shard allowance and trigger re-probing.

rachel: good guard. action items: rachel to draft RFC with the shard allocator design and config schema; omar builds sim traces and runs A/B variants; tessa to define UI/telemetry surface and acceptance checks; zane to prototype prober prefix caps and eviction counters. target: RFC v0.1 Wednesday EOD, sim results Thurs.

infra-bot: deploy note: probe-shard-sim env created -> prebench staging queue attached.

rachel: thanks all. please drop any corner cases here (e.g., per-customer SLAs, extreme seqlen variance). :thumbsup:
